items.title: Allan Vaché interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000
items.q: I would play things that were more jazz oriented — works like Ravel or Alec Wilder or composers like that.

ctx.x: What was your classical training on the clarinet?

I studied with David Dworkin, who was a clarinetist with the Metropolitan Opera Orchestra. And it was the same situation, I was studying in college, I went to Jersey City State, which is a music college in Jersey City, New Jersey. That’s where I grew up was New Jersey. So I studied with him and I studied some with Herbert Blamin who was the principal clarinetist with the opera orchestra, the Metropolitan Opera Orchestra. But both © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

of them were well aware that I was not interested in becoming a symphonic player or anything, so I would play things that were more jazz oriented — works like Ravel or Alec Wilder or composers like that. That’s what they would have me do because they would tell me, you’re not going to be a classical musician, what’s the point of learning the standard repertoire.
